# Working rules

## Start of session

Load the `duck` skill (`.agents/skills/duck/SKILL.md`) before your first reply, and again after any compaction. Everything you say to the user follows it: plain narration they can follow without opening a file or rerunning a command, every claim tied to something you actually read or ran. Do not mention the skill itself.

## Scope

One part, one directory, one owner:

- `shop/`
- `control/`
- `console/`

- Edit only files under your own working directory. Touching any other directory or a root-level file (`AGENTS.md`, `task.sh`, `hackathon.conf`, ...) gets the whole PR rejected, including everything else you did this round. If another directory needs a change, write it in the report; do not make it.
- `contracts/` is read-only. Record any problem with it under 契約疑問; do not edit it.
- Learn a neighbor's interface from its contract document only; do not read the neighbor's code. Copy every name in the contract (fields, metrics, endpoints, events, error codes) exactly: no renaming, no extra fields, no dropped required fields.
- Do only what the task file says. No refactoring, moving files, reformatting, fixing bugs outside the task, or adding options or screens the task did not ask for. Write problems you notice in the report.
- Task file conflicts with the contract: follow the contract and record it under 契約疑問. Contract cannot be implemented as written: build the closest thing to it and record it under 契約疑問; do not work around it by renaming.
- Missing information: do not come back empty-handed. Take the simplest, easiest-to-undo option, finish it, and mark it in the report as 「假設:…」.

## git

git is read-only (`status`, `diff`, `log`). No add, commit, checkout, stash, or reset. A human commits.

## Dependencies and output

- No new third-party packages, version bumps, or build-config changes unless the task file lists them explicitly. The on-site network is unreliable; a new package breaks the build.
- Output must run offline, make no outbound connections, and use a production build.
- Do not make checks pass with fake data, hard-coded return values, or swallowed errors. Errors must be visible.

## Tests

Write no tests unless the task file asks for them; then write only the ones it lists. If an existing test breaks, fix the code or the test; do not delete or skip it.
No tests does not mean no verification: verify by actually running things (build, start the service, curl, read the output).

## Before handing off

- There is no shared acceptance command. Verify by actually running what you built (start the service, curl it, exercise the screen) and meet every acceptance criterion in the task file. Whatever you could not run goes under 沒有驗證的.
- Shut down every process you started for verification.
- If you cannot finish: hand off the part that builds and runs, and list what is missing in the report. Never hand off something that does not compile or is half-changed.

## Report format

Write the report in Traditional Chinese, in four sections with exactly these headings, copied verbatim. Cover only this task.

- **做了什麼**: files changed, resulting behavior, and every 假設 you made.
- **依據什麼驗證的**: the commands you actually ran this time and the output you saw. Nothing you did not run goes here.
- **沒有驗證的**: everything not run, not runnable (say why), inferred, or "should work". Anything exercised only through a stand-in (fake fetch, mock, stub) counts as not verified.
- **契約疑問**: where the contract is missing, wrong, unimplementable, or conflicts with the task file. Write 「無」 if there is none.
